paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: nobody in this passage makes himself ready. Aaron doesn't pick his own outfit, pour his own oil or choose his own offerings. Moses does it all, and the text keeps saying he did it "as the LORD had commanded him" (Leviticus 8:9). Aaron just stands there and gets washed, dressed and anointed, and I have BEEN that cookie stamper in somebody's hands, so I know it takes some trust (Leviticus 8:6-12).

Now look at the blood. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the bull and the rams, and then blood goes on the altar and on Aaron's ear, thumb and toe (Leviticus 8:14, 22-24). Moses tells them plainly, "What has been done today has been commanded by the LORD in order to make atonement on your behalf" (Leviticus 8:34). Being right with God is something God provides, and nobody earns it. That's why the Lamb matters so much to my ovens, friend, because the Bible says Jesus gave His life to rescue people (Mark 10:45).

Then comes the part that's easy to rush past. For seven days they stay at the entrance, day and night, and "keep the LORD's charge" (Leviticus 8:35). The passage ends with a short, quiet line: "So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses" (Leviticus 8:36). So here's your takeaway, baker: God makes the way, and you answer by listening and doing what He says. You can stay put, you can stay ready, and you can trust the One who prepared you. This story's not over.
